explanation: Gleason–Montgomery–Zippin (1952): a locally Euclidean (Hausdorff) topological group is a Lie group; this is the 'commonly cited solution' of Hilbert's fifth problem referred to on Wikipedia (Hilbert–Smith conjecture) and van den Dries–Goldbring. The statement takes a Hausdorff topological group G with a ChartedSpace structure over ℝ^n on its own topology and asserts a LieGroupPresentation G n: a homeomorphic group isomorphism onto a Hausdorff real-analytic Lie group of the same dimension n. No second countability is required, which is consistent with GMZ (a local result). Faithful.
